contentEn:
Vancouver homeowners ask Reno Stars one question more than any other when planning a bathroom renovation: what does it actually cost per square foot? The short answer in 2026 is $200 to $560 per square foot, depending on scope, property type and finish level. That range is not pulled from a contractor brochure — it comes from 23 real Reno Stars bathroom renovation projects across Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, North Vancouver, Coquitlam, Delta and Maple Ridge.

Understanding cost per square foot helps you set a realistic budget before you meet with a contractor. It also lets you compare quotes accurately, because some contractors quote by the job and others quote by the foot. Reno Stars provides both figures in every initial estimate, so you can see exactly how your project stacks up against real completed work in your city.

How Vancouver Bathroom Renovation Cost Per Square Foot Is Calculated

Cost per square foot is derived by dividing the total contract price by the finished bathroom's area. Reno Stars calculates this for every project at the budgeting stage, and it varies most by three factors. First is the scope of work: a basic update with new tiles, a vanity and a toilet costs far less per square foot than a full gut renovation that moves plumbing lines. Second is finish level — a mid-range renovation with a quartz countertop and porcelain tile sits in a different price tier than a luxury curbless shower with heated floors and custom millwork. Third is property type: a condo bathroom in a Vancouver highrise has different structural constraints than a basement bathroom in a Richmond townhouse, which affects labour time and permit requirements.

Labour accounts for roughly 55 to 65 percent of the total cost in most Vancouver bathroom renovations. Materials make up the remaining 35 to 45 percent, with finish selections — tile, fixtures, vanity — being the largest variable. Reno Stars itemises both line items in every proposal so you know exactly where your money goes.

Bathroom Renovation Cost Per Square Foot by Property Type

Condo bathrooms in Vancouver tend to be smaller — typically 35 to 70 square feet — but the per-square-foot cost runs higher than larger bathrooms because minimum trade costs are spread across fewer square feet. Reno Stars' smallest condo bathroom project in 2025 was a 45-square-foot master bath in Vancouver at $14,000 to $16,000, working out to $311 to $356 per square foot.

Townhouse bathrooms fall in the middle range. A daughter's bath renovation in Richmond — roughly 80 square feet — came in at $17,000 to $20,000, or $212 to $250 per square foot. A dual bathroom renovation with a powder room in Richmond, covering approximately 110 square feet total, was $33,000 to $35,000 — $300 to $318 per square foot. The wider spread reflects scope differences: a powder room has less plumbing complexity than a full bath with a custom-tiled shower.

Single-family home bathrooms generally have more flexibility for high-end finishes because homeowners are already invested in the property. A two-bathroom renovation in Burnaby — roughly 160 combined square feet — ran $26,000 to $30,000, or $162 to $187 per square foot. A master bathroom renovation with custom features in Vancouver, approximately 80 square feet, was $14,000 to $16,000 — $175 to $200 per square foot. These figures illustrate why larger combined bathrooms often cost less per square foot than smaller isolated ones: the minimum trade costs are distributed across more area.

What Drives Bathroom Renovation Cost Per Square Foot in Vancouver

The highest per-square-foot costs in the dataset come from two project types: small luxury bathrooms and three-bathroom renovations in townhouses. The Delta three-bathroom project — $40,000 to $43,000 for roughly 80 square feet — reflects the minimum trade cost reality in multi-bathroom renovations. When three bathrooms are renovated together, each one still requires its own minimum plumbing, electrical and tiling setup, so the total contract is high even though the per-bathroom square footage is modest.

The North Vancouver luxury curbless shower project — $42,000 to $45,000 for approximately 80 square feet — illustrates how premium finishes compound cost per square foot. A curbless shower requires structural modification to lower the floor, waterproofing the entire bathroom floor plane, custom glass, and often a linear drain. These features add $8,000 to $15,000 to a renovation that might otherwise cost $20,000 to $25,000, pushing the per-square-foot figure from the mid-$200s into the $500s.

Mid-range renovations at $200 to $300 per square foot are the most common scope for Vancouver homeowners who are upgrading for personal use rather than resale. These typically include a new bathtub or walk-in shower, standard porcelain or ceramic tile, a solid-surface countertop, updated plumbing fixtures and fresh paint. Reno Stars' project data shows that most Burnaby and Richmond bathroom renovations fall into this tier.

How to Use Cost Per Square Foot When Planning Your Bathroom Renovation

Cost per square foot is most useful as a planning benchmark, not a firm quote. The reason: minimum costs set a floor. A tiny 35-square-foot condo bathroom in Vancouver cannot be renovated for $7,000 — no matter what the per-square-foot math suggests — because a contractor still needs to rent equipment, bring in a plumber and electrician, and order a minimum quantity of tile and waterproofing material. The minimum viable cost for any Vancouver bathroom renovation in 2026 is approximately $12,000 to $14,000, regardless of size.

When reviewing quotes, ask your contractor for the cost-per-square-foot breakdown alongside the total. This makes it easier to compare across quotes that cover different scopes. If one quote is $22,000 for an 80-square-foot bathroom and another is $28,000, the per-square-foot figure ($275 vs $350) tells you the price difference is about finish level, not scope — something a total-price comparison alone does not reveal.

Reno Stars includes a detailed cost-per-square-foot breakdown in every initial estimate, with line items for labour, materials and permits. This lets Vancouver homeowners see exactly what each decision — upgrading from porcelain to natural stone tile, or adding a second vanity — adds to the total per square foot.

Permit Requirements for Bathroom Renovations in Greater Vancouver

Most bathroom renovations in Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond and other municipalities within Greater Vancouver do not require a building permit if the work does not alter structural elements, change the location of plumbing fixtures, or affect fire separations. Replacing a bathtub with a walk-in shower, updating tile and flooring, and installing a new vanity generally fall under renovation permits — not building permits — which are typically handled by the contractor as part of the project scope.

If your bathroom renovation includes moving plumbing lines — relocating a toilet, adding a second drain, or converting a powder room to a full bath — a building permit is required in all Metro Vancouver municipalities. Permit costs in Vancouver typically range from $400 to $1,200 depending on the scope and municipality. Reno Stars obtains all necessary permits as part of the project agreement, so homeowners do not need to submit applications separately.

Strata approval is required for any renovation work in condominiums and townhouses in British Columbia, regardless of permit requirements. This is a separate approval from the municipal building permit and is typically initiated by the contractor with the strata management company. Reno Stars has experience navigating strata approval processes across Greater Vancouver municipalities and includes this coordination in the project timeline.

Frequently Asked Questions — Bathroom Renovation Cost Per Square Foot Vancouver

What is the average bathroom renovation cost per square foot in Vancouver in 2026?

Based on 23 Reno Stars bathroom renovation projects across Greater Vancouver, the average cost per square foot in 2026 ranges from $200 to $350 per square foot for mid-range renovations. Luxury renovations with curbless showers, heated floors and premium finishes run $450 to $560 per square foot. Condo bathrooms smaller than 50 square feet often exceed $300 per square foot because minimum trade costs are spread across fewer square feet.

Why do small bathrooms cost more per square foot than large ones?

Small bathrooms cost more per square foot because every renovation has fixed minimum costs: a plumber and electrician must attend regardless of bathroom size, waterproofing must cover the entire floor area, and permit and disposal fees are charged at a flat rate. These minimum costs — typically $8,000 to $12,000 in combined trade minimums — are a larger percentage of a small project's total budget. Reno Stars' smallest 2025 project, a 45-square-foot condo bathroom in Vancouver, cost $311 to $356 per square foot, compared to $162 to $187 per square foot for a 160-square-foot two-bathroom renovation in Burnaby.

Does Vancouver's climate affect bathroom renovation cost?

Yes. Vancouver's wet climate means bathroom waterproofing standards are higher than in drier regions. Proper moisture management, mold-resistant backer board and adequate ventilation are standard requirements in Vancouver bathroom renovations, not optional upgrades. These requirements add approximately $800 to $2,000 to the overall project cost depending on bathroom size, but they protect the home from the moisture damage that is common in older Vancouver properties with inadequate bathroom ventilation.

How long does a bathroom renovation take in Vancouver?

A standard bathroom renovation in Vancouver typically takes three to five weeks from demolition to final inspection. Condo renovations may take slightly longer due to strata approval timelines and restricted work hours. Multi-bathroom renovations completed together generally take five to eight weeks. Reno Stars provides a detailed project schedule with every proposal, including trade sequencing, permit timelines and inspection dates.

Is a bathroom renovation worth the cost per square foot for resale?

bathroom renovations in Vancouver typically recoup 60 to 80 percent of their cost in increased property value, according to reno ROI data from the Canadian RENOVA Awards and regional resale comparables. A renovated bathroom in Vancouver is one of the highest-ROI improvements for homeowners planning to sell within five years. Even a mid-range renovation that costs $18,000 to $22,000 can add $25,000 to $40,000 to a Vancouver home's assessed value, depending on the property and neighbourhood.

2026年溫哥華洗手間裝修每平方英尺的成本是多少？答案是每平方英尺200至560加元，具體取決於工程範圍、房產類型和裝修檔次。這個數字並非來自承包商的宣傳冊，而是來自聚星裝修在溫哥華、本拿比、列治文、北溫、和高貴林完成的23個真實洗手間裝修項目。

了解每平方英尺的成本有助於業主在與承包商會面之前設定合理的預算。聚星裝修在每份初步報價中同時提供兩種計價方式，讓您準確比較不同項目之間的成本效益。

成本計算方式

每平方英尺的裝修成本是將合同總價除以已完成洗手間的面積。成本差異主要由三個因素決定：工程範圍（基本更新與全面翻新差異很大）、裝修檔次（瓷磚、衛生潔具、櫥櫃的選擇），以及房產類型（公寓衛生間與獨立屋洗手間的結構限制不同）。

真實項目數據

以下為聚星裝修2025至2026年完成的洗手間裝修項目成本明細。所有價格均包含人工、材料及許可證費用。

  • 溫哥華公寓主人浴室定制裝修 — $14,000至$16,000，約45平方英尺， 每平方英尺$311至$356
  • 高贵林標准淋浴改造 — $14,000至$17,000，約60平方英尺，每平方英尺$233至$283
  • 列治文女兒浴室灰瓷磚裝修 — $17,000至$20,000，約80平方英尺，每平方英尺$212至$250

  • 北溫無障礙豪華淋浴浴室 — $42,000至$45,000，約80平方英尺，每平方英尺$525至$562

影響成本的主要因素

每平方英尺成本最高的項目往往是小型豪華浴室和聯排別墅的多浴室翻新。三浴室翻新項目的合同總價較高，因為每個浴室仍需獨立的管道、電力和瓷磚的最低配置成本。North Vancouver的無障礙淋浴項目展示了豪華裝修如何提高每平方英尺的成本：無障礙淋浴需要結構修改、整個浴室地板的防水處理、定制玻璃和線性地漏，這些功能將原本約$20,000至$25,000的裝修推向$500以上的每平方英尺水平。

許可證要求

在大溫哥華大多數洗手間翻新工程不需要建築許可證，前提是工程不改變結構、不移動管道設施或不影響防火隔離。將浴缸更換為步入式淋浴、鋪設瓷磚和安裝新洗臉盆通常屬於裝修許可證範圍，由承包商辦理。如需移動管道線路，則需要建築許可證。聚星裝修作為項目協議的一部分代為辦理所有必要的許可證。

常見問題

2026年溫哥華洗手間裝修每平方英尺的平均成本是多少？

根據聚星裝修在大溫哥華地區的23個洗手間裝修項目數據，2026年中檔裝修每平方英尺的平均成本為200至350加元。配備無障礙淋浴、暖氣地板和豪華裝修的項目為每平方英尺450至560加元。面積小於50平方英尺的公寓洗手間通常超過每平方英尺300加元。

為什麼小浴室每平方英尺的成本更高？

小型洗手間每平方英尺成本更高，是因為每次翻新都有固定的最低成本：水管工和電工無論浴室大小都必須到場，防水必須覆蓋整個地板區域，許可證和處理費用按固定費率收取。

溫哥華的氣候會影響洗手間裝修成本嗎？

是的。溫哥華潮濕的氣候意味著洗手間防水標準比乾燥地區更高。正確的防潮管理、防霉水泥板和充分通風是溫哥華洗手間翻新的標准要求，而非可選升級。

洗手間翻新需要多長時間？

溫哥華標准洗手間翻新通常需要三到五週時間。公寓裝修可能因共管公寓審批流程和受限工作時間而稍長。

洗手間翻新是否值得投資？

洗手間翻新通常能收回成本的60%至80%。即使是花費$18,000至$22,000的中檔翻新工程，也可能為溫哥華住宅增加$25,000至$40,000的評估價值。
